text: In nineteen twenty-seven, a professor started an experiment that nobody has ever seen happen.
Thomas Parnell wanted to prove that something solid could secretly be a liquid.
So he took pitch, a tar so hard it shatters like glass under a hammer.
He melted it into a funnel, and waited three years for it to settle.
Then he cut the bottom open. And waited.
Eight years later, one drop fell.
Nine years later, another. About one drop a decade.
Luckily, it got a devoted new guardian, John Mainstone, who watched it for fifty-two years.
Unluckily, he never saw a drop fall.
Once, he missed it by a day.
Once, he stepped out for a drink, and missed it by five minutes.
Then they finally pointed a camera at it, and the drop fell during a twenty-minute power cut.
You see, pitch really is a liquid, just over two hundred billion times thicker than water.
Think of cold honey, then give it a few decades.
The experiment even won an Ig Nobel Prize.
In twenty thirteen, John Mainstone passed away, still waiting.
And here's the twist: the next drop never really fell. It touched the pile below, and only broke off when somebody bumped the jar.
